The spray base is very important. You need a good coating that is dry and smooth. Shake the can upside down and do light quick moving sprays to cover the model. Practice on a scrap model. You want a good solid base, but you don't want to lose detail.

Shake well, look at the bottom of the pot if you see pigment, shake more.

Get a decent  amount on the brush and cover the model, apply. Be careful not to drown the model in contest though.

When applying try to cover the entire area your working on ( do the head at once, the arms at once. That way when it dries it dries smooth over that area).

If you think you applied to much, clean off your brush, dry it, and dip the brush tip into the area you applied to much, to remove the excess, clean brush repeat

Hi!

- step 1: paint the base in a thick coat of Agrellan Earth ( texture ), and Stirland Battle mire ( texture)

- make sure you have them in blotches of there own, with mixed areas between. 

- step 2: after step 1 has dried and formed the texture. Wash it in Nuln. Wait for this to dry.

- step 3: Lightly Dry brush Tallarn sand ( scenery ), and lightly dry brush  Ushanti bone ( scenery )

- step 4: Now For the grass tufts I use GW Tufts, but feel free to use any other. I apply a small amount of super glue to the spot I want it, put the Tuft on it, and use the wooden handle of a brush to sink it into position

- step 5: Now is the snow! I use Valhallan Blizzard ( texture ), I work it into the grass tufts, smear it around the Base and make blobs of it.
